item.title: Hollywood unions lock in AI guardrails as tech firms urge industry slowdown
item.description:
Hollywood unions lock in AI guardrails as tech firms urge industry slowdown

Hollywood unions and writers have secured enforceable guardrails for generative AI in entertainment, while heads of major AI companies are calling for an industry‑wide slowdown.

🔍 Overview

  • AI models that generate digital facsimiles of actors and replicate traditional filmmaking tools “pose a threat to some human jobs.”
  • The AI tools used in entertainment production differ from the AI systems that have sparked recent whistleblowing and apocalyptic declarations.
  • Anthropic alignment lead Evan Hubinger warned the technology could “kill all humans” within the next decade.

🛡️ Union Negotiations

  • SAG‑AFTRA chief negotiator Duncan Crabtree‑Ireland said the union recognized early on how AI could impact its members’ livelihoods.
  • “We bargained for and achieved enforceable, meaningful guardrails around how this technology can be implemented by the major employers in our industry,” Crabtree‑Ireland explained.
  • The guardrails do not include companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google directly, but do cover all U.S. entertainment content creators.
  • WGAE executive director Sam Wheeler condemned the “tech oligarchs pushing AI on our society.”
  • The WGAE has long warned that unregulated artificial intelligence poses an existential threat to workers, to our democracy, and to the world.
  • Guild members have bargained meaningful AI protections into their contracts; in 2023 WGA members spent 148 days on strike before studios agreed to real safeguards for film and television writers.

⚙️ Industry Response

  • Hollywood unions’ fight for strict rules around generative AI did not stop the entertainment industry from embracing AI.
  • Alliance of Motion Picture and Television Producers (AMPTP) has been reluctant to adopt demands such as requiring studios to gain permission and compensate actors for AI‑generated replicas.
  • Crabtree‑Ireland noted that without the principle of compensation, “the economic incentive to use replication and to replace human performances would have been much stronger” and would have resulted in “a much greater and faster adoption of digital replication.”

🚨 Risks & Concerns

  • AI‑generated digital replicas threaten certain acting and filmmaking jobs.
  • Prominent AI leaders (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, X) have called for an industry‑wide slowdown on the technology’s development.

🏛️ Political Context

  • President Donald Trump dismissed AI concerns as overreactions.
  • Some other U.S. politicians have felt pressured to take legislative action.

Source: What Hollywood thinks about existential AI warnings

item.title: Industry Leaders and Historians Call for AI Regulation and Caution
item.description:
Industry Leaders and Historians Call for AI Regulation and Caution

Prominent technology executives and researchers are advocating for the regulation of artificial intelligence, citing long-term risks and the need for proactive government oversight.

💡 Why it matters

Concerns regarding autonomous systems date back several decades:

  • In 1863, Samuel Butler warned that intelligent self-replicating machines could replace humans.
  • In 1951, Alan Turing stated that undying machines would eventually “take control” and “outstrip our feeble powers.”
  • In 2000, Bill Joy described self-replicating robots as potentially more dangerous than nuclear weapons.

⚙️ Key details

Various industry leaders have called for specific regulatory actions and precautions:

Person Position/Affiliation Stated View or Action
Elon Musk X CEO / OpenAI Investor Called AI “potentially more dangerous than nukes” and said we must be “proactive about regulation instead of reactive.”
Sundar Pichai Google CEO Stated “there is no question in my mind that artificial intelligence needs to be regulated.”
Brad Smith Microsoft President Opened the door to voluntary regulation in a speech at the Brookings Institution.
Mark Zuckerberg Meta Founder Suggested his company should be regulated following the Cambridge Analytica scandal.
Eric Horvitz Microsoft Chief Scientific Officer Led researchers in 2009 to consider policies to constrain behaviors of autonomous systems.

Additionally, a letter published by the Future of Life Institute and signed by Musk, among others, stated that if a pause on AI cannot be enacted quickly, “governments should step in and institute a moratorium.”

#AI #Regulation #TechPolicy #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: A brief history of AI executives calling for regulation

item.title: President Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang During All-In Summit
item.description:
President Trump Calls Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang During All-In Summit

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang received a phone call from President Trump while onstage at the All-In Podcast’s All-In Summit on Monday. Huang placed the president on speakerphone to address the live audience.

🔍 Overview

During the live call, President Trump addressed concerns regarding the future of artificial intelligence. He described recent fears about AI development as a “hoax” and stated that “the robots will not be taking over.”

⚙️ Key details

  • President Trump’s comments followed an essay by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, which advocated for slowing AI development and increasing government coordination.
  • In response to the discourse, President Trump stated that he intends to push back against the current narrative surrounding AI risks.
  • The president also remarked on the economic impact of data centers, claiming they have turned struggling communities into wealthy ones.

💡 Why it matters

Following the president’s statements, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang commented on the future of the industry:

Participant Stance on AI Future
President Trump The robots will not be taking over
Jensen Huang We’re going to make sure that everybody wins in the AI race in America

Huang further stated that he intends for every industry, company, state, and individual to benefit from the AI race in America.

#Nvidia #AI #JensenHuang #TechPolicy #AllInSummit

Source: Jensen Huang puts Trump on speakerphone onstage to announce robots won’t take over the world
